(Japanese: '''ウパーがいっぱい！''' ''Lots of {{tt|Upah|Wooper}}!'') is the 148th episode of the [[Pokémon animated series]]. It was first broadcast in Japan on May 18, 2000, and in the United States on March 31, 2001. {{spoilers}} ==Blurb== Ash and friends enthusiastically volunteer to watch over a troubled trainer's school of Wooper. But as always Team Rocket interferes, this time hoping to use the Wooper's soothing qualities to pacify Giovanni. ==Plot== Crossing a hill on the way to [[Goldenrod City]], {{Ash}} and {{ashfr}} notice a building nearby. As {{an|Brock}} is about to say what he thinks the building is, a {{p|Wooper}} drops from a tree and lands on Brock's neck, causing him to fall down the slope. On the lower level, [[Olesia]] is about to teach the class of {{p|Wooper}} when Brock hits the ground. Wooper jumps off Brock and Olesia asks if he is alright. Brock quickly recovers and starts flirting with her. {{an|Misty}} pulls him away and asks Olesia about the buildings. Olesia explains that she loved to raise Wooper, so she went on to build [[Pokémon Day Care|the Wooper Pond preschool]] only for Wooper. Ash consults his [[Pokédex]] for information on Wooper, which reminds him of his [[EP127|previous encounter]] with the {{p|Quagsire}}. Misty asks Olesia if they could watch her teach and she agrees. She plays the tambourine and the Wooper start to swim and dance. Ash and Misty admire the cuteness of the Wooper while Brock admires Olesia. In the woods, [[Jessie]] is looking around for food when she finds a mushroom. After [[James]] and {{MTR}} tell her that it is poisonous, she tosses it aside and all three start to complain of how they haven't had any food for weeks. Then James says that they could call "{{an|Giovanni|the Boss}}" for money but Meowth reminds him that they have already spent all the money. They decide their only hope is to find a rare Pokémon. {{TP|Jessie|Wobbuffet}} pops out of his {{i|Poké Ball}}, but Jessie quickly [[recall]]s him. Ash and his friends enjoy some tea and homemade biscuits with Olesia, but the picnic is interrupted when Olesia receives a call from her mom. Olesia is left concerned by the phone call and confirms with Ash's group that her mother has broken her leg after falling down some stairs. Brock offers to take care of the Wooper while she is away. She accepts, gives Brock a book about raising Wooper, and drives off on her motorcycle. Ash and his friends head inside the preschool's gates only to discover that the Wooper aren't in the pond. {{AP|Pikachu}} finds a trail of water that leads into one of the school's buildings. They follow the trail and find the Wooper eating and all over the place. Brock reads in the book that the best way to get Wooper to listen is to show them affection and food. So Brock pulls out a piece of [[Pokémon food]] and shows it to the Wooper. One Wooper walks up to Brock and proceeds to licking him, and soon the others follow suit. Ash reads that the second best way was to play the tambourine. Misty recalls that she used to play the tambourine when she was a little girl. She picks up the tambourine and begins to play it, but none of the Wooper seem to be entertained. As such, she puts the instrument down and {{TP|Misty|Togepi}} begins to play it instead. The Wooper are instantly swaying and follow Togepi to their outdoor pond. Misty is angry that they'd rather listen to Togepi's beat rather than her own. Brock says it's just because Pokémon know a Pokémon's beat. After all the Wooper have been returned to the pond, Brock congratulates Togepi on a job well done, and is relieved to have recovered all the Wooper. However, Misty realizes that one Wooper is missing; more specifically, Olesia's favorite one with a love heart marking on its chest. Brock is shocked by the revelation and goes on to jingle the tambourine for the enjoyment of the Wooper. Misty and Ash leave Brock in charge of Togepi and the Wooper while they search for the missing one. As Ash and Misty look in one of the rooms a loud crash in the kitchen catches their attention. The crash came from the missing Wooper, however, just as Ash and Misty are about to retrieve it, it runs away, dodging all their attempts to catch it and almost destroying the room in the process; Ash and Misty hurry to stop a large pile of plates toppling over, and Pikachu is almost stabbed by falling cutlery, this results in the Wooper getting away. Outside, the Wooper is seen climbing the cliff face Brock fell down. Ash and Misty once again give chase. Wooper reaches the top of the cliff before Ash and Misty do, and runs off into the forest. It is later spotted crossing a very rickety rope bridge across a chasm. Ash runs across but is frozen with fear when hearing the creaking beams beneath his feet, Misty and Pikachu tentatively follow. Misty tries to reason with the Wooper to return to the pond, Wooper agrees, and begins jumping up and down in excitement. This makes the bridge begin to wobble, and once again the Wooper slips through their grasp and runs across to the other side of the bridge. The bridge breaks leaving Ash and Misty hanging and Pikachu on the top having made it across. Ash tells Pikachu to leave them and chase the Wooper. Meanwhile, {{MTR}} is seen complaining over a boiling pot, claiming that mushroom soup won't have much flavor without any mushrooms. He notices the Wooper, and, mistaking it for a mushroom, attempts to catch it. Jessie and James return from their foraging, and, hearing about the "giant mushroom", start looking around for it, while the Wooper eats from their basket of mushrooms. They spot the "giant mushroom" just as it eats the last of their mushrooms. The trio is at first angered by the Wooper, but its smiling face gets rid of this anger. Jessie decides it would be a good idea to take it for their boss, thinking that Wooper's overwhelming cuteness may cause Giovanni to forget about their many failures. Jessie throws out a Poke Ball, but it fails as Wooper already has a {{pkmn|Trainer}}. Pikachu arrives to Wooper's defense, and refuses {{TRT}}'s request to convince the Wooper to enter the Poké Ball for them. Ash and Misty rush onto the scene. Team Rocket reveal their nets and soon everyone is scrambling to grab Wooper, but its slippery skin is making it a difficult task. Jessie commands Wobbuffet to attack the [[twerp]]s, but he does nothing. She sends {{TP|Jessie|Arbok}} clashing into the group, and James orders his {{TP|James|Weezing}} to use {{m|Smokescreen}}. Team Rocket escapes in their [[Team Rocket's mechas|balloon]] with Wooper netted, but at that moment Olesia and Brock arrive on a motorbike to give chase. Team Rocket recites their {{motto}}. Before Brock and the others release their Pokémon to free the Wooper, Olesia thinks she can entice it to return by telling it that playtime is over and it has to go back inside. Wooper promptly jumps out of the net and back to the group as Arbok and Weezing pursue it. Wooper looks in trouble, but Olesia commands it to use {{m|Tackle}} attack on both of them, revealing it to be a strong Wooper. On command, Wooper tosses Arbok into Weezing, and the hurtling Pokémon collide with the rest of Team Rocket before being blasting off. Back at the school, Togepi had been keeping the group entertained with its tambourine. Brock asks what Olesia's secret is for raising such strong Pokémon, to which she replies that there isn't one, and the strength really comes from people not expecting the Wooper to be powerful. Brock asks if he can stay at the school so they can both learn about Pokémon and "maybe each other", resulting in him getting dragged away by Misty. The group says their goodbyes, and continues on their way through [[Johto]]. ==Major events== * [[Jessie]] attempts to {{pkmn2|caught|catch}} a {{p|Wooper}}, but fails, as it already has a {{pkmn|Trainer}}. {{animeevents|GS}} ===Debuts=== ====Pokémon debuts==== * {{p|Wooper}} ==Characters== ===Humans=== [[File:Dare da EP148.png|thumb|200px|{{tt|Dare da?|Who's That Pokémon?}}]] * {{Ash}} * {{an|Misty}} * {{an|Brock}} * [[Jessie]] * [[James]] * [[Olesia]] ===Pokémon=== [[File:WTP EP148.png|thumb|200px|Who's That Pokémon?]] [[Who's That Pokémon?]]: {{p|Skarmory}} ''(US and international)'', {{p|Wooper}} ''(Japan)'' * {{p|Pikachu}} ({{OP|Ash|Pikachu}}) * {{p|Meowth}} ({{TRM}}) * {{p|Togepi}} ({{OP|Misty|Togepi}}) * {{p|Wobbuffet}} ({{OP|Jessie|Wobbuffet}}) * {{p|Arbok}} ({{OP|Jessie|Arbok}}) * {{p|Weezing}} ({{OP|James|Weezing}}) * {{p|Wooper}} ([[Olesia]]'s; multiple; debut) * {{p|Quagsire}} (flashback) {{right clear}} ==Trivia== * The episode's English [[dub]] title is based on the phrase "big whoop". * This episode was partially adapted into the book [[Ash to the Rescue]]. * The [[GS Ball]] appears in a flashback in this episode, marking its last appearance in the {{pkmn|animated series}}. * This episode marks the first time {{TP|Jessie|Wobbuffet}} pops out of his {{i|Poké Ball}}. * Music from ''[[PK01|Pikachu's Vacation]]'' can be heard in this episode. ===Errors=== * The [https://www.pokemon.com/us/animation/seasons/3/episode-43-no-big-woop/ corresponding page] on [[Pokémon.com]] used to list the synopsis for the previous episode instead of this episode. * At the end of the episode, the narrator states, "Our heroes are headed once again for new adventures on their journey ''to'' [[Johto]]." However, they are already in Johto. * In the beginning of the episode, {{an|Brock}} calls [[Olesia]] by her name before she introduces herself. * In the scene where Brock attempts to control the {{p|Wooper}}, he holds a pellet of food in his hand. After the Wooper overpower him, the pellet is gone. * After [[James]] puts the basket of mushrooms down, he should have noticed the Wooper because it appeared next to the basket in such a small time frame in which it is seen and when James is seen walking away. * {{p|Wooper}} uses {{m|Tackle}}, a move that it [[Animated series move errors|cannot legally learn in the games]]. * In the Brazilian Portuguese dub, [[James]] is completely silent when he tries to catch {{p|Wooper}} with his hands. ===Dub edits=== * [[Pokémon Karaokémon]]: [[Pikachu (I Choose You)]] * In the Latin American dub, James mentions ''La vecindad del Chavo'' from the popular Mexican TV show ''El Chavo del Ocho''. ==In other languages== {{Epilang|color={{colorschemelight|GS}}|bordercolor={{colorschemedark|GS}} |ar={{tt|هروب ووبر|Wooper's escape}} |bg={{tt|Малкият Упър!|Tiny Wooper}} |zh_cmn={{tt|好多烏波！|So many Wooper}} |cs={{tt|Malý, ale silný|Small but strong}} |nl={{tt|Klein Maar Fijn|Small but Beautiful}} |de={{tt|Die Felino-Schule|The Wooper-school}} |fr_eu={{tt|Fugueur à faire peur|A runaway to cause fear}} |he=קטן אבל חזק{{tt|katan aval chazak|Small but strong}} |hu=Bébicsőszök csődközelben |it={{tt|Così piccoli eppure così forti|So tiny yet so strong}}{{tt|*|Original 2000 dub}}
